title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Start with a rational Hodge structure (V_Q, V_C = ⊕ V^{pq}). Let G be its Mumford–Tate group, so G_C ⊂ Aut_C(V). Add a k-structure V_k ⊂ V_C for a subfield k ⊂ C, chosen so that the Hodge filtration F^p is defined over k. This is exactly the shape of the Betti and de Rham data of a motive over k, together with its comparison isomorphism. Page 29 had just recast the data a)–g) of a motivic Galois group as ⊗-categories of exactly such objects V(V_Q, ⊕V^{ij}, V_k).

Question. When does a triple (V_Q, ⊕V^{pq}, V_k ⊂ V_C) come from a motive over k? Grothendieck derives necessary conditions.

Step 1. If the triple is motivic, its motivic Galois group G' is a k-group: the ⊗-automorphisms of the de Rham fibre functor T_DR.

Step 2. Assume the Hodge conjecture. Then motivic cycles and Hodge classes coincide, so G' becomes the Mumford–Tate group after extending scalars to C (identity components when k is not algebraically closed).

Step 3. Hence the Mumford–Tate group must be definable over k through the given k-structure V_k ⊂ V_C. He calls this 'loin d'être triviale' (far from trivial).

Step 4. Equivalent tensor form: every G-invariant tensor (Hodge tensor) in ⊗^n(V^∨ ⊗ V) must be rational in the corresponding tensor space over k', for some finite extension k'/k. When k is algebraically closed, rational over k itself. This is precisely the requirement that Hodge classes be de Rham-rational over k̄, the de Rham half of Deligne's later notion of 'absolute Hodge'.

Step 5. He notes these conditions are very restrictive but certainly not sufficient. Counterexample: k = Q with V_k = V_Q, i.e. de Rham and Betti lattices coincide, so all periods are rational. This is in general impossible; think of Q(1), whose period is 2πi.

Step 6. The next page draws the conclusion: one must add conditions 'du type conjecture de transcendance' (of transcendence-conjecture type), i.e. what is now Grothendieck's period conjecture.

Overall, the page tries to characterise the essential image of the realisation functor {motives over k} → {Hodge structures with a k-de Rham structure} by Tannakian invariants plus transcendence. In modern terms: 'which Hodge–de Rham structures are motivic?'
errors: The equality is written G'_C = G°_C, but the identity component belongs on the motivic side. The Mumford–Tate group is connected, so G° = G. Over a non-algebraically-closed k the motivic Galois group G' is in general disconnected. The correct statement is (G')°_C = G_C, which agrees with what he writes for k algebraically closed: G'_C = G_C.

The tensor criterion (Hodge tensors are k'-rational in the de Rham structure) captures only the identity component, i.e. the situation over k̄. Fully describing G' over k would also require the Galois action on these tensors; he gestures at this with the finite extension k' but leaves it unspelled.
The whole argument is conditional on the Hodge conjecture. He states this, and it is not a logical error.

ideas.what: Necessary condition for a Hodge structure with a k-de Rham structure to be motivic over k: the Mumford–Tate group must descend to k via V_k. Equivalently, all Hodge tensors are rational over k̄ (a finite extension of k) in the de Rham realisation.
ideas.modern_name: de Rham rationality of Hodge classes / absolute Hodge cycles (de Rham component); motivic Galois group compared with the Mumford–Tate group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, LNM 900, 1982); the comparison of the motivic Galois group with the MT group is Serre/Deligne/Saavedra (1970s)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted orally/through Saavedra's thesis and Deligne; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Identifying the motivic Galois group with the Mumford–Tate group under the Hodge conjecture.
ideas.modern_name: G_mot(M)_C ≅ MT(M) (identity component) under the Hodge conjecture
ideas.where_published: unsure; standard folklore attributed to Grothendieck via Saavedra/Serre

ideas.what: Tannakian invariants are insufficient (counterexample k = Q, V_k = V_Q), so transcendence conditions on periods must be added.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period conjecture (trdeg of the period field = dim of the motivic Galois group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', 1966; formalised by André, Une introduction aux motifs, 2004)
ideas.where_published: Publ. IHES 29 (1966), footnote on 2πi / periods; the 1965 notes here are an earlier and more structural formulation

ideas.what: Problem of characterising the essential image of the motives → Hodge–de Rham structures functor over a subfield k ⊂ C.
ideas.modern_name: 'Which Hodge structures are motivic?' (Hodge-theoretic analogue of Fontaine–Mazur)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed by Deligne, Simpson, Green–Griffiths–Kerr; no standard conjecture

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out, already in 1965, to characterise motivic Hodge–de Rham triples over k by two kinds of necessary conditions. The first is Tannakian: the Mumford–Tate group descends to k, i.e. Hodge tensors are k̄-rational in de Rham. The second is transcendence-type period conditions. This implicitly asks whether the two together are also sufficient. That 'Hodge-theoretic Fontaine–Mazur' question is not standardly attributed to him and remains open and seldom formulated.
missed.quote: il faut que G°_C soit définissable sur k via V_k ⊂ V_C ; ceci une condition loin d'être triviale ! ... Elles ne sont certainement pas suffisantes en général.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work on periods (Ayoub, André, Huber–Müller-Stach on period conjectures) and on motivic Hodge structures could take up this precise combination of conditions as a candidate characterisation of motivic objects.

missed.claim: The requirement that Hodge classes be rational over k̄ in de Rham cohomology appears here as a necessary consequence of the Hodge conjecture. This is the de Rham part of Deligne's later 'absolute Hodge' notion, here 17 years before Deligne's 1982 work.
missed.quote: élément de ⊗^n(V'⊗V) invariant sous G ... est rationnel dans ⊗^n_{k'}(V'_{k'}⊗V_{k'}) ; ∃ extension finie k' de k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: it shows Grothendieck already saw de Rham rationality of Hodge classes as the key arithmetic constraint linking Hodge theory and motives.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (MT group equals motivic Galois group under Hodge, de Rham rationality of Hodge classes, period conjecture) are known and partly attributed to Grothendieck. What is notable is the early, explicit framing as necessary conditions for a converse 'which Hodge–de Rham structures are motivic' problem, combining absolute-Hodge-type rationality with transcendence conditions in 1965.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the main text: 'Soit V_k ⊂ V_C une restriction des scalaires de C à k ⊂ C, compatible avec la filtration naturelle de V_C' is correct; 'restriction' here means a k-form / descent of V_C.
'le groupe G' déf/k, [?] à T_DR' likely reads 'le groupe G' déf/k des ⊗-automorphismes de T_DR' or 'associé à T_DR'.
'est rationnel [?] dans ⊗_{k'}...' is likely 'soit rationnel sur k' dans ...'.
'dans [?] ∃ extension finie' likely 'il doit exister une extension finie k' de k'.
The struck parenthetical after 'G'_C = G°_C' appears to be a cancelled remark, perhaps '(conj. de Hodge)'.
Last line: '[Exemple k = Q, V_k = V_Q, ce n'est en général pas possible ...]' seems right; it is bracketed in the original and continues onto the next page.
